## Sampler Diagnostics {#sec-supp-sampler}

@tbl-supp-sampler reports the Hamiltonian Monte Carlo diagnostics of each chain [@betancourtConceptualIntroductionHamiltonian2017]: the adapted step size, the mean number of leapfrog steps per iteration, how often the trajectory hit the maximum tree depth, divergent transitions, and the energy Bayesian fraction of missing information, E-BFMI [@betancourtDiagnosingSuboptimalCotangent2016].

```{r}
#| label: tbl-supp-sampler
#| tbl-cap: "Sampler diagnostics by chain. E-BFMI below 0.2 would indicate that the momentum resampling cannot move the chain across energy levels fast enough; the maximum tree depth is 10."
ebfmi <- function(E) sum(diff(E)^2) / sum((E - mean(E))^2)
sampler_tab <- imap_dfr(sup, function(fit, nm) {
  d <- posterior::as_draws_df(fit$diag) |> as_tibble()
  tm <- fit$time$chains
  d |>
    group_by(Chain = .chain) |>
    summarise(`Step size` = fmt(mean(stepsize__), 3), `Leapfrog steps` = fmt(mean(n_leapfrog__), 1),
              `Max depth` = max(treedepth__), `At max depth` = sum(treedepth__ >= fit$metadata$max_treedepth),
              Divergent = sum(divergent__), `E-BFMI` = fmt(ebfmi(energy__), 2), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(`Warm-up (s)` = fmt(tm$warmup, 1), `Sampling (s)` = fmt(tm$sampling, 1),
           Fit = ifelse(Chain == 1, fit_lab[[nm]], "")) |>
    select(Fit, Chain, everything())
})
sampler_tab |> ktab(align = "lrrrrrrrrr")
div_total <- sum(sampler_tab$Divergent)
maxdepth_total <- sum(sampler_tab$`At max depth`)
ebfmi_min <- min(as.numeric(sampler_tab$`E-BFMI`))
```

Neither fit has `r if (div_total == 0) "a single divergent transition" else paste(div_total, "divergent transitions")`, `r if (maxdepth_total == 0) "no iteration reaches" else paste(maxdepth_total, "iterations reach")` the maximum tree depth, and the smallest E-BFMI is `r fmt(ebfmi_min, 2)`, far above 0.2. @fig-supp-energy compares the marginal energy distribution with the distribution of energy changes between iterations; overlapping histograms are what a healthy fit looks like.

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-energy
#| fig-cap: "Energy diagnostic. Grey: marginal energy $E$, centred; orange: the change in energy between successive iterations, $\\Delta E$. Pooled over chains."
#| fig-scap: "HMC energy diagnostic"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.34
imap_dfr(sup, function(fit, nm) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(fit$diag) |> as_tibble() |>
    group_by(.chain) |>
    mutate(`E (centred)` = energy__ - mean(energy__), `Delta E` = c(NA, diff(energy__))) |>
    ungroup() |> select(`E (centred)`, `Delta E`) |>
    pivot_longer(everything()) |> mutate(fit = fit_short[[nm]])
}) |>
  filter(!is.na(value)) |>
  ggplot(aes(value, fill = name)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 60, position = "identity", alpha = 0.55) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`E (centred)` = col_ref, `Delta E` = col_power)) +
  facet_wrap(~fit, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Density")
```

## Convergence {#sec-supp-convergence}

@tbl-supp-conv gives posterior summaries and convergence diagnostics of the structural parameters: the rank-normalised split-$\widehat R$ [@gelmanInferenceIterativeSimulation1992; @vehtariRankNormalizationFoldingLocalization2021], bulk and tail effective sample sizes [@geyerPracticalMarkovChain1992], and the Monte Carlo standard error of the posterior mean.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-supp-conv
#| tbl-cap: "Posterior summaries and convergence diagnostics for the structural parameters. \\emph{MCSE} is the Monte Carlo standard error of the posterior mean."
conv <- imap_dfr(sup, function(fit, nm) {
  posterior::summarise_draws(fit$par, "mean", "sd", q5 = \(x) quantile(x, 0.05, names = FALSE),
                             q95 = \(x) quantile(x, 0.95, names = FALSE), "rhat", "ess_bulk", "ess_tail", "mcse_mean") |>
    mutate(fit = nm)
})
conv |>
  filter(variable %in% names(pm_use)) |>
  mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = names(pm_use))) |>
  arrange(factor(fit, levels = c("first", "final")), variable) |>
  mutate(variable = as.character(variable),
         Fit = ifelse(variable == names(pm_use)[1], fit_lab[fit], ""), Parameter = var_tex[variable],
         across(c(mean, sd, q5, q95), \(x) fmt(x, 2)),
         `$\\widehat R$` = fmt(rhat, 3), `ESS bulk` = fmt(ess_bulk), `ESS tail` = fmt(ess_tail), MCSE = fmt(mcse_mean, 3)) |>
  select(Fit, Parameter, Mean = mean, SD = sd, `5\\%` = q5, `95\\%` = q95, `$\\widehat R$`, `ESS bulk`, `ESS tail`, MCSE) |>
  ktab(align = "llrrrrrrrr")
worst <- conv |> slice_min(ess_bulk, n = 1)
mcse_ratio <- max(conv$mcse_mean / conv$sd)
```

Every structural $\widehat R$ is at most `r fmt(max(conv$rhat), 3)`, and the smallest bulk effective sample size is `r fmt(worst$ess_bulk)`, for `r sym_list(worst$variable)` in the `r tolower(sub(".*, ", "", fit_lab[[worst$fit]]))` fit. Monte Carlo standard errors are at most `r pct(mcse_ratio, 1)` of the posterior standard deviations. The team strengths are too many to tabulate; @fig-supp-rhat-ess shows the distribution of their $\widehat R$ and of their bulk effective sample size per draw.

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-rhat-ess
#| fig-cap: "Convergence of all team strengths $r_i$. Left: rank-normalised $\\widehat R$, with the gate at 1.01. Right: bulk effective sample size per draw; values above one are possible for anti-correlated chains, which NUTS often produces for well-identified parameters."
#| fig-scap: "Convergence of all team strengths"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.36
imap_dfr(sup, function(fit, nm) {
  posterior::summarise_draws(fit$r, "rhat", "ess_bulk") |>
    transmute(`R-hat` = rhat, `Bulk ESS / draws` = ess_bulk / S_draws, fit = fit_short[[nm]])
}) |>
  pivot_longer(-fit) |>
  ggplot(aes(value, fill = fit)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40, position = "identity", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_vline(data = tibble(name = "R-hat", g = 1.01), aes(xintercept = g), linetype = "dashed", colour = col_power) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = col_fit) +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Teams")
```

Trace plots (@fig-supp-trace) show the chains iteration by iteration; rank plots (@fig-supp-rank) rank the draws of all chains together, and if the chains sample the same distribution each chain's ranks are uniform [@vehtariRankNormalizationFoldingLocalization2021]. Autocorrelation (@fig-supp-acf) should damp quickly with the lag, and the Gelman--Rubin shrink factor (@fig-supp-gr) should fall to 1 as the chains lengthen and stay there [@gelmanInferenceIterativeSimulation1992].

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-trace
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Trace plots of the structural parameters, ", fit_lab[["final"]], " (top block) and ", fit_lab[["first"]], ". One shade of grey per chain.")'
#| fig-scap: "Trace plots"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 1.2
imap_dfr(sup, \(fit, nm) par_long(fit) |> mutate(fit = factor(fit_short[[nm]], levels = rev(fit_short)))) |>
  ggplot(aes(.iteration, value, colour = factor(.chain))) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.12, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = chain_greys, guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(fit ~ variable, scales = "free_y", ncol = 5, labeller = labeller(variable = label_parsed, fit = label_wrap_gen(14))) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Iteration (post-warm-up)", y = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-rank
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Rank plots of the structural parameters for both fits. For each parameter the draws of all chains are ranked jointly and each chain''s ranks are binned into 20 bins; the band is the central 95\\% range of a bin count under uniformity. Lines are chains; ", fit_lab[["first"]], " in orange, ", fit_lab[["final"]], " in grey.")'
#| fig-scap: "Rank plots"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.75
nb <- 20
band <- qbinom(c(0.025, 0.975), S_draws / n_chains, 1 / nb)
imap_dfr(sup, function(fit, nm) {
  par_long(fit) |> group_by(variable) |>
    mutate(bin = ceiling(rank(value, ties.method = "random") / (n() / nb))) |>
    count(variable, .chain, bin) |> mutate(fit = nm)
}) |>
  ggplot(aes(bin, n, group = interaction(.chain, fit), colour = fit)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 0.5, xmax = nb + 0.5, ymin = band[1], ymax = band[2], fill = col_faint, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_step(linewidth = 0.3, direction = "mid", alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(first = col_power, final = col_ink), guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~variable, ncol = 5, labeller = label_parsed) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Rank bin", y = "Draws per bin")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-acf
#| fig-cap: "Autocorrelation of the structural parameters up to lag 20, averaged over chains. Orange: first Monday; grey: final."
#| fig-scap: "Autocorrelation"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.55
acf_df <- imap_dfr(sup, function(fit, nm) {
  par_long(fit) |> group_by(variable, .chain) |>
    reframe(lag = 0:20, acf = as.numeric(stats::acf(value, lag.max = 20, plot = FALSE)$acf)) |>
    group_by(variable, lag) |> summarise(acf = mean(acf), .groups = "drop") |> mutate(fit = nm)
})
acf_df |>
  ggplot(aes(lag, acf, colour = fit)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = col_faint) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.5) + geom_point(size = 0.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(first = col_power, final = col_ink), guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~variable, ncol = 5, labeller = label_parsed) +
  labs(x = "Lag", y = "Autocorrelation")
damp <- acf_df |> group_by(fit, variable) |> summarise(lag10 = suppressWarnings(min(lag[abs(acf) < 0.1])), .groups = "drop")
slow <- damp |> slice_max(lag10, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
slow_var <- names(pm_use)[match(as.character(slow$variable), pm_use)]
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-gr
#| fig-cap: "Gelman--Rubin shrink factor (rank-normalised split-$\\widehat R$) of each structural parameter computed on the first $n$ post-warm-up iterations of every chain, as $n$ grows. The dashed line is the gate at 1.01."
#| fig-scap: "Gelman--Rubin shrink factor against iteration"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.45
gr_df <- imap_dfr(sup, function(fit, nm) {
  arr <- fit$par
  ns <- unique(round(seq(50, posterior::niterations(arr), length.out = 25)))
  map_dfr(ns, function(n) {
    sub_arr <- posterior::subset_draws(arr, iteration = seq_len(n))
    tibble(n = n, variable = posterior::variables(arr),
           rhat = map_dbl(posterior::variables(arr), \(v) posterior::rhat(posterior::extract_variable_array(sub_arr, v))))
  }) |> mutate(fit = fit_short[[nm]])
})
gr_df |>
  ggplot(aes(n, rhat, group = variable)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, colour = col_faint) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1.01, linetype = "dashed", colour = col_power) +
  geom_line(colour = col_ink, linewidth = 0.35, alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~fit) +
  labs(x = "Iterations per chain", y = expression(hat(R)))
gr_ok <- gr_df |> group_by(fit, n) |> summarise(m = max(rhat), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(fit) |> summarise(n_ok = min(n[m <= 1.01]), .groups = "drop")
```

The autocorrelation of `r sum(damp$lag10 <= 3)` of the `r nrow(damp)` parameter--fit pairs drops below 0.1 within three lags; the slowest is `r sym_list(slow_var)` in the `r tolower(sub(".*, ", "", fit_lab[[slow$fit]]))` fit, which needs `r slow$lag10` lags. The shrink factors of every parameter are below the gate after `r fmt(max(gr_ok$n_ok))` iterations per chain in both fits and stay there.

## Posterior Geometry {#sec-supp-geometry}

Hierarchical models have funnels: when a scale parameter such as $\omega$ or $\tau$ is small, the effects it governs must be close to their mean, and the posterior narrows into a region the sampler can struggle to enter. The non-centred parameterisation of @eq-hier removes the funnel from the sampled coordinates when the data are weak [@papaspiliopoulosGeneralFrameworkParametrization2007]. @fig-supp-pairs plots each scale against a standardised effect it governs, in the sampled coordinates; divergent transitions, if any, would be drawn in orange.

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-pairs
#| fig-cap: "Posterior geometry in the sampled coordinates, 1,000 draws per panel: the conference effect $u_c$ of the first conference against $\\log\\omega$, and the team effect $z_i$ of the team with the fewest games against $\\log\\tau$. Divergent transitions would be orange."
#| fig-scap: "Posterior geometry of the hierarchical scales"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.62
geom_df <- imap_dfr(sup, function(fit, nm) {
  p <- posterior::as_draws_df(fit$par) |> as_tibble()
  d <- posterior::as_draws_df(fit$diag) |> as_tibble()
  cr <- unclass(posterior::as_draws_matrix(fit$conf_raw))
  zz <- unclass(posterior::as_draws_matrix(fit$z))
  team_few <- which.min(games_of(fit))
  set.seed(1)
  keep <- sample.int(nrow(p), 1000)
  bind_rows(
    tibble(x = cr[keep, 1], y = log(p$sigma_conf[keep]), panel = "log(omega) ~ u[c]"),
    tibble(x = zz[keep, team_few], y = log(p$sigma_team[keep]), panel = "log(tau) ~ z[i]")
  ) |> mutate(div = rep(d$divergent__[keep], 2) == 1, fit = fit_short[[nm]])
})
geom_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x, y)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = div), size = 0.5, alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = col_ink, `TRUE` = col_power), guide = "none") +
  facet_grid(fit ~ panel, scales = "free", labeller = labeller(panel = label_parsed)) +
  labs(x = "Standardised effect", y = "Log scale")
```

Neither fit shows a funnel in the sampled coordinates: the standardised effects have the same spread at every value of the scale. In the final fit the team effect is concentrated, because a full season pins the team down; on the first Monday it spreads more widely. The random walk has a funnel of the same kind, between $\phi$ and the standardised steps of @eq-walk, which is not drawn; the evidence that the sampler enters its neck is the absence of divergent transitions together with the informative prior that keeps $\phi$ away from zero.

## Prior and Posterior {#sec-supp-prior}

@fig-supp-prior-post overlays the prior density of each structural parameter on its posterior in both fits, and @fig-supp-contraction condenses the comparison into two numbers per parameter [@schadPrincipledBayesianWorkflow2021]: the posterior contraction $1 - \Var_{\text{post}}/\Var_{\text{prior}}$, near one when the data dominate the prior, and the posterior $z$-score $(\E_{\text{post}} - \E_{\text{prior}})/\mathrm{sd}_{\text{post}}$.

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-prior-post
#| fig-cap: "Prior (dashed) and posterior densities of the structural parameters. Priors are normal, truncated to the parameter's support; $\\eta$ has the prior of the season."
#| fig-scap: "Prior and posterior densities"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.8
prior_spec <- pri |> filter(variable %in% names(pm_use)) |>
  mutate(lower = ifelse(variable %in% c("hca", "kappa", "b_prev2"), -Inf, 0), upper = ifelse(variable == "b_prev", 1.2, Inf))
prior_dens <- function(x, a, b, lower, upper) ifelse(x > lower & x < upper, dnorm(x, a, b) / (pnorm(upper, a, b) - pnorm(lower, a, b)), 0)
post_long <- imap_dfr(sup, \(fit, nm) par_long(fit) |> mutate(fit = fit_short[[nm]]))
rng_p <- post_long |> group_by(variable) |> summarise(lo = quantile(value, 0.0005), hi = quantile(value, 0.9995), .groups = "drop")
prior_curves <- prior_spec |>
  mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = names(pm_use), labels = pm_use)) |>
  inner_join(rng_p, by = "variable") |>
  rowwise() |>
  reframe(variable = variable, { x <- seq(lo - 0.15 * (hi - lo), hi + 0.15 * (hi - lo), length.out = 300)
                                 tibble(x = x, dens = prior_dens(x, mean, sd, lower, upper)) })
ggplot() +
  geom_density(data = post_long, aes(value, fill = fit, colour = fit), alpha = 0.35, linewidth = 0.3, adjust = 1.2) +
  geom_line(data = prior_curves, aes(x, dens), linetype = "dashed", colour = col_power, linewidth = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = col_fit) + scale_colour_manual(values = col_fit) +
  facet_wrap(~variable, scales = "free", ncol = 5, labeller = label_parsed) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Density")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-contraction
#| fig-cap: "Posterior contraction against posterior $z$-score for the structural parameters, for both fits. Prior moments are those of the truncated priors."
#| fig-scap: "Posterior contraction and z-scores"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.55
tn_moments <- function(m, s, a, b) {
  al <- (a - m) / s; be <- (b - m) / s
  Z <- pnorm(be) - pnorm(al)
  dal <- ifelse(is.finite(al), dnorm(al), 0); dbe <- ifelse(is.finite(be), dnorm(be), 0)
  aal <- ifelse(is.finite(al), al * dnorm(al), 0); bbe <- ifelse(is.finite(be), be * dnorm(be), 0)
  c(m + s * (dal - dbe) / Z, s^2 * (1 + (aal - bbe) / Z - ((dal - dbe) / Z)^2))
}
pmom <- prior_spec |> rowwise() |>
  mutate(pm = tn_moments(mean, sd, lower, upper)[1], pv = tn_moments(mean, sd, lower, upper)[2]) |>
  ungroup() |> select(variable, pm, pv)
contraction <- conv |> inner_join(pmom, by = "variable") |>
  mutate(contraction = 1 - sd^2 / pv, z = (mean - pm) / sd, fit = fit_short[fit], lab = pm_use[variable])
contraction |>
  ggplot(aes(contraction, z, colour = fit)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = col_faint) +
  geom_point(size = 1.6) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = lab), parse = TRUE, size = 2.8, seed = 1, show.legend = FALSE, min.segment.length = 0) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = col_fit) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(NA, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Posterior contraction", y = "Posterior z-score")
low_c <- contraction |> filter(fit == fit_short[["first"]], contraction < 0.5)
low_f <- contraction |> filter(fit == fit_short[["final"]], contraction < 0.5)
hi_z <- contraction |> filter(abs(z) > 2)
```

On the first Monday, `r nrow(low_c)` of `r n_distinct(contraction$variable)` structural parameters contract by less than half`r if (nrow(low_c)) paste0(" --- ", sym_list(low_c$variable), " ---") else ""` so their priors carry the fit, as intended in a week with two games per team. `r if (nrow(low_f) == 0) "By the end of the season every parameter contracts by more than half." else paste0("By the end of the season every parameter except ", sym_list(low_f$variable), " contracts by more than half: the pooled priors are about as informative as a season.")` `r if (nrow(hi_z) == 0) "No posterior lies more than two of its own standard deviations from its prior mean." else paste0("Posteriors more than two of their own standard deviations from the prior mean are ", paste0("$", sym_lab[hi_z$variable], "$ (", c("First Monday" = "first Monday", Final = "final")[hi_z$fit], ", $z = ", fmt(hi_z$z, 1), "$)", collapse = "; "), ": for these the prior is centred away from where the data put them, but is too wide to pull them back.")`

## Justification of the Informative Priors {#sec-supp-justify}

Informative priors need a justification that does not come from the data they are applied to. Ours come from the history of the sport. The `prior_refits` target refits the final posterior of every complete season, each with about 5,500 games, under deliberately vague priors --- $\eta \sim \mathcal N(0, 10^2)$, $\beta \sim \mathcal N(0.5, 1)$ on $(0, 1.2)$, $\beta_2 \sim \mathcal N(0, 1)$, half-normal priors with scale 10 on $\omega$ and $\tau$, scale 2 on $\lambda$ and $\kappa$ (normal for $\kappa$) and scale 50 on $\sigma_e$ and $\sigma_m$, and $\phi \sim \mathcal N^+(0.5, 0.5^2)$, wide but centred away from zero, because under a prior with its mode at zero the sampler stalls in the random walk's funnel (@sec-hierarchy) --- so that a season's estimate owes nothing to the published priors; the chains are twice as long as the published ones. @fig-supp-justify plots the resulting per-season posteriors against the priors in use, and @tbl-supp-justify gives the numbers.

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-justify
#| fig-cap: "Per-season full-season posteriors under vague priors (points: mean; bars: $\\pm 2$ posterior sd) against the prior in use (line: prior mean; bands: $\\pm 1$ and $\\pm 2$ prior sd)."
#| fig-scap: "Per-season posteriors against the priors"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.75
pri_band <- pri |> filter(variable %in% names(pm_use)) |>
  mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = names(pm_use), labels = pm_use))
refits |>
  filter(variable %in% names(pm_use)) |>
  mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = names(pm_use), labels = pm_use)) |>
  ggplot(aes(season, mean)) +
  geom_rect(data = pri_band, aes(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = mean - 2 * sd, ymax = mean + 2 * sd), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            fill = col_power, alpha = 0.10) +
  geom_rect(data = pri_band, aes(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = mean - sd, ymax = mean + sd), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            fill = col_power, alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_hline(data = pri_band, aes(yintercept = mean), colour = col_power, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = mean - 2 * sd, ymax = mean + 2 * sd), colour = col_ref, linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(size = 1, colour = col_ink) +
  facet_wrap(~variable, scales = "free_y", ncol = 5, labeller = label_parsed) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2016, 2020, 2024), labels = \(x) substr(sl(x), 6, 7)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-supp-justify
#| tbl-cap: "Empirical basis of the priors: the pooled mean of the per-season full-season posterior means under vague priors, their between-season standard deviation (DerSimonian--Laird), the typical within-season posterior sd (root mean square), the predictive sd of @eq-pool, and the prior in use. \\emph{LOSO} is the share of seasons whose own estimate lies within two standard deviations of the prior pooled from the other seasons, counting the estimate's own posterior sd. Only the first four priors are pooled; the rest are weakly informative."
loso_cov <- loso_z |> group_by(variable) |> summarise(cov = mean(abs(z) <= 2)) |> (\(d) setNames(d$cov, d$variable))()
pooled |>
  inner_join(pri |> select(variable, mean, sd), by = "variable") |>
  mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = pri$variable)) |>
  arrange(variable) |>
  transmute(Parameter = var_tex[as.character(variable)], `Pooled mean` = fmt(pooled_mean, 2),
            `Between-season sd` = fmt(between_sd, 2), `Posterior sd` = fmt(typical_post_sd, 2),
            `Predictive sd` = fmt(predictive_sd, 2), Prior = sprintf("$\\mathcal N(%s, %s^2)$", fmt(mean, 2), fmt(sd, 2)),
            LOSO = pct(loso_cov[as.character(variable)])) |>
  ktab(align = "lrrrrlr")
```

Two points qualify this justification. First, pooling every complete season is empirical Bayes at the level of the sport, and saying that a season's estimate lies inside a prior partly built from it would be circular. The last column of @tbl-supp-justify avoids that: for each season it pools the *other* seasons only and asks whether the season's own estimate lies within two standard deviations of that leave-one-season-out prior. For the four pooled parameters it does in `r if (min(loso_cov[pooled_vars], na.rm = TRUE) == 1) "every season" else paste0(pct(min(loso_cov[pooled_vars], na.rm = TRUE)), " or more of seasons")`, so a new season should be expected to fall inside its prior. Second, the prior standard deviation removes estimation noise from the between-season spread (@eq-pool): for parameters whose between-season spread is no larger than estimation noise alone would produce, the prior is as narrow as the uncertainty of a mean over a dozen seasons. That is the right width if the parameter is the same every season, and the leave-one-season-out column checks it.

## Induced Priors {#sec-supp-induced}

A prior on parameters induces a prior on everything computed from them, and a set of individually reasonable priors can combine into an unreasonable one. The quantities that matter here are not $\omega$ or $\tau$ but the spread of team strengths, the probability that the home team wins an even game, and the distribution of margins the model expects before seeing any game. @tbl-supp-induced simulates them from the priors alone, on the `r sl(last_full)` schedule with its preseason predictions, each game played at the random-walk states of its period and its margin drawn from the model.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-supp-induced
#| tbl-cap: !expr 'paste0("Induced priors, by simulation from the priors alone (", fmt(nrow(ip$draws)), " draws) on the ", sl(last_full), " schedule and preseason predictions. The last column gives the value observed in ", sl(last_full), " where one exists.")'
ind_lab <- c(
  sigma_game = "Margin scale $\\bar\\sigma$ (per 100, 70 possessions)",
  r2 = "Share of margin variance from efficiency, $R^2$",
  tau = "Weekly random-walk step $\\phi$",
  sd_rating = "SD of team strengths (per 100)",
  top_minus_45 = "Best minus 45th-best team (per 100)",
  p_home_even = "P(home win), evenly matched teams",
  p_top_vs_avg = "P(best team beats an average one), neutral",
  sd_margin = "SD of regulation margin (points)",
  within3 = "Share of games within 3 points",
  home_win = "Home regulation win rate, home floor"
)
ip$draws |>
  select(all_of(names(ind_lab))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything()) |>
  group_by(name) |>
  summarise(q05 = quantile(value, 0.05), q50 = median(value), q95 = quantile(value, 0.95), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(obs = ip$observed[name], name = factor(name, levels = names(ind_lab))) |>
  arrange(name) |>
  transmute(Quantity = ind_lab[as.character(name)], `5\\%` = fmt(q05, 2), Median = fmt(q50, 2),
            `95\\%` = fmt(q95, 2), Observed = ifelse(is.na(obs), "", fmt(obs, 2))) |>
  ktab(align = "lrrrr")
ipq <- function(v, p) quantile(ip$draws[[v]], p, names = FALSE)
ip_lab <- c(sd_margin = "SD of margin", within3 = "Share within 3 pts", home_win = "Home win rate")
ip_in <- map_lgl(names(ip_lab), \(v) ip$observed[[v]] >= ipq(v, 0.025) & ip$observed[[v]] <= ipq(v, 0.975))
```

The induced priors are on the scale of the sport: before any game, the model expects the best team to be about `r fmt(ipq("top_minus_45", 0.5), 0)` points per 100 better than the 45th (90\% prior interval `r fmt(ipq("top_minus_45", 0.05), 0)`--`r fmt(ipq("top_minus_45", 0.95), 0)`), an even game to be won at home `r pct(ipq("p_home_even", 0.5))` of the time, and margins with a standard deviation of about `r fmt(ipq("sd_margin", 0.5), 0)` points. `r if (sum(ip_in) == length(ip_in)) "All three" else paste(sum(ip_in), "of the three")` observed statistics lie inside the central 95\% of their prior predictive distribution`r if (!all(ip_in)) paste0("; the exception is the ", paste(tolower(ip_lab[!ip_in]), collapse = " and "), "") else ""`. The prior on $\bar\sigma$, which sets every win probability and therefore every $\pi_g$ in the resume, is induced by three separate weakly informative priors and is wide (90\% interval `r fmt(ipq("sigma_game", 0.05), 1)`--`r fmt(ipq("sigma_game", 0.95), 1)`); the data narrow it to a few tenths in any snapshot after the first week.

## Posterior Predictive Checks {#sec-supp-ppc}

@sec-ppc compared summary statistics with their replicates. Here the whole distributions are compared (@fig-supp-dens), then the predictive distribution of each game without that game, by the leave-one-out probability integral transform.

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-dens
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Observed distribution (black) against 50 replicated data sets (orange) for the ", fit_lab[["final"]], " fit. Left: regulation margin in points, replicated from the marginal law of @eq-lik-marg and rounded. Right: efficiency margin per 100 live possessions, for games that have one.")'
#| fig-scap: "Posterior predictive densities"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.4
fin <- sup$final
rep_long <- bind_rows(
  as_tibble(t(fin$yrep[1:50, ]), .name_repair = \(n) paste0("r", seq_along(n))) |>
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "rep") |> mutate(signal = "Regulation margin (points)"),
  as_tibble(t(fin$erep[1:50, ]), .name_repair = \(n) paste0("r", seq_along(n))) |>
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "rep") |> mutate(signal = "Efficiency margin (per 100)")
)
obs_long <- bind_rows(tibble(value = fin$obs, signal = "Regulation margin (points)"),
                      tibble(value = fin$eff, signal = "Efficiency margin (per 100)"))
ggplot() +
  geom_density(data = rep_long, aes(value, group = rep), colour = col_power, alpha = 0.2, linewidth = 0.2, bw = 2) +
  geom_density(data = obs_long, aes(value), colour = col_ink, linewidth = 0.7, bw = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~factor(signal, levels = c("Regulation margin (points)", "Efficiency margin (per 100)")), scales = "free") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-50, 50)) +
  labs(x = "Home minus away", y = "Density")
```

The density overlay shows the misfit of @sec-ppc directly: the observed margin has a spike at zero, the overtime games, that no replicate has. The leave-one-out probability integral transform (LOO-PIT) checks calibration game by game: for each game, $\Pr(y_g^{\text{rep}} \le y_g \mid \text{all other games})$, estimated with the Pareto-smoothed importance weights of the LOO computation. If the model is calibrated these values are uniform; a U shape indicates predictive distributions that are too narrow, a hump that they are too wide [@gabryVisualizationBayesianWorkflow2019; @sailynojaGraphicalTestDiscrete2022]. @fig-supp-pit shows them for both signals and both fits.

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-pit
#| fig-cap: "LOO-PIT histograms, 20 bins; the band is the central 95\\% range of a bin count under uniformity. The margin's PIT uses its marginal law; the spike of regulation ties sits at the PIT value of zero margin, which depends on the game."
#| fig-scap: "LOO-PIT histograms"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.6
pit_df <- imap_dfr(sup, function(fit, nm) {
  bind_rows(tibble(pit = fit$pit_margin, signal = "Regulation margin"), tibble(pit = fit$pit_eff, signal = "Efficiency margin")) |>
    filter(!is.na(pit)) |> mutate(fit = fit_short[[nm]])
}) |> mutate(signal = factor(signal, levels = c("Regulation margin", "Efficiency margin")))
pit_band <- pit_df |> count(fit, signal) |>
  mutate(lo = qbinom(0.025, n, 1 / 20) / (n / 20), hi = qbinom(0.975, n, 1 / 20) / (n / 20))
pit_df |>
  ggplot(aes(pit)) +
  geom_rect(data = pit_band, aes(xmin = 0, xmax = 1, ymin = lo, ymax = hi), inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = col_faint, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.05), fill = col_power, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, colour = col_ink, linewidth = 0.3) +
  facet_grid(signal ~ fit) +
  labs(x = "LOO-PIT", y = "Density")
pit_out <- pit_df |> mutate(bin = pmin(floor(pit * 20) + 1, 20)) |> count(fit, signal, bin) |>
  left_join(pit_df |> count(fit, signal, name = "N"), by = c("fit", "signal")) |>
  mutate(out = n < qbinom(0.025, N, 0.05) | n > qbinom(0.975, N, 0.05)) |>
  summarise(out = sum(out), bins = n())
```

Of the `r pit_out$bins` histogram bins across the four panels, `r pit_out$out` fall outside their 95\% band, against about `r fmt(0.05 * pit_out$bins, 0)` expected by chance. @fig-supp-resid plots the observed margin minus its posterior mean against that mean; a systematic trend would mean that the model's spreads are biased for lopsided or for close matchups --- for example, if strong favourites won by less than predicted.

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-resid
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Residual regulation margin (points) against the posterior mean margin, ", fit_lab[["final"]], ". The line is a LOESS smooth with a 95\\% band.")'
#| fig-scap: "Residuals against predicted margin"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.45
tibble(mu = fin$mu_mean, resid = fin$obs - fin$mu_mean) |>
  ggplot(aes(mu, resid)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = col_faint) +
  geom_point(size = 0.4, alpha = 0.3, colour = col_ink) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", colour = col_power, fill = col_power, alpha = 0.2, linewidth = 0.7) +
  labs(x = "Posterior mean margin (points)", y = "Observed minus mean (points)")
```

## Influence and PSIS Diagnostics {#sec-supp-loo}

The Pareto $\hat k$ of each game estimates the tail shape of its importance ratios in PSIS-LOO; values above 0.7 mean the leave-one-out approximation is unreliable for that game, and in practice that the game is highly influential [@vehtariParetoSmoothedImportance2024]. @fig-supp-khat plots every game's $\hat k$ in both fits.

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-khat
#| fig-cap: "Pareto $\\hat k$ for each game, in schedule order. Dashed lines at 0.5 and 0.7."
#| fig-scap: "Pareto k diagnostics"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.4
imap_dfr(sup, \(fit, nm) tibble(game = seq_along(fit$loo$diagnostics$pareto_k), k = fit$loo$diagnostics$pareto_k, fit = fit_short[[nm]])) |>
  ggplot(aes(game, k)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(0.5, 0.7), linetype = "dashed", colour = col_power, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(size = 0.5, alpha = 0.6, colour = col_ink) +
  facet_wrap(~fit, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Game", y = expression(hat(k)))
k_first <- sum(sup$first$loo$diagnostics$pareto_k > 0.7)
k_final <- sum(fin$loo$diagnostics$pareto_k > 0.7)
k_first5 <- sum(sup$first$loo$diagnostics$pareto_k > 0.5)
```

`r k_final` of `r fmt(fin$n_games)` games exceed 0.7 in the final fit and `r k_first` of `r fmt(sup$first$n_games)` on the first Monday (`r k_first5` above 0.5). Early in the season a single game is a large share of the evidence about two teams, so removing it moves their posteriors more, but with two games per team and a strong preseason prediction no game is the only evidence about anyone.

## Power-scaling Sensitivity {#sec-supp-powerscale}

@tbl-sens summarised power-scaling sensitivity by a single distance per parameter. @fig-supp-powerscale shows what lies behind it for the parameters flagged most often: the posterior density as the prior (top row) or the likelihood (bottom row) is raised to powers between 0.8 and 1.25 [@kallioinenDetectingDiagnosingPrior2024]. A density that shifts with the prior power is prior-sensitive; one that shifts with the likelihood power is informed by the data.

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-powerscale
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Power-scaled posterior densities, ", fit_lab[["final"]], ". Darker lines are larger powers $\\alpha$; the base posterior is $\\alpha = 1$.")'
#| fig-scap: "Power-scaled posterior densities"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.55
ps <- fin$powerscale
flag_vars <- flag_counts |> filter(variable %in% names(pm_use)) |> arrange(desc(conflict + weak), desc(prior)) |> slice_head(n = 5) |> pull(variable)
if (!is.null(ps)) {
  get_side <- function(side_list, side) {
    map_dfr(side_list, function(d) {
      a <- attr(d, "powerscaling")$alpha
      posterior::as_draws_df(d) |> as_tibble() |> select(any_of(flag_vars), any_of(".log_weight")) |> mutate(alpha = a)
    }) |> mutate(side = side)
  }
  base <- posterior::as_draws_df(ps$base_draws) |> as_tibble() |> select(any_of(flag_vars)) |> mutate(alpha = 1)
  sides <- bind_rows(get_side(c(ps$prior_scaled$draws_sequence), "Prior scaled"),
                     get_side(c(ps$likelihood_scaled$draws_sequence), "Likelihood scaled"))
  sides <- bind_rows(sides, mutate(base, side = "Prior scaled"), mutate(base, side = "Likelihood scaled"))
  if (!".log_weight" %in% names(sides)) sides$.log_weight <- 0
  sides |>
    mutate(.log_weight = coalesce(.log_weight, 0)) |>
    group_by(side, alpha) |> mutate(w = exp(.log_weight - max(.log_weight)), w = w / sum(w)) |> ungroup() |>
    pivot_longer(any_of(flag_vars), names_to = "variable") |>
    mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = names(pm_use), labels = pm_use),
           side = factor(side, levels = c("Prior scaled", "Likelihood scaled"), labels = c("Prior~scaled", "Likelihood~scaled"))) |>
    ggplot(aes(value, weight = w, group = alpha, colour = alpha)) +
    geom_density(linewidth = 0.35, adjust = 1.3) +
    scale_colour_gradient(low = "gray80", high = col_power, name = expression(alpha)) +
    facet_wrap(side ~ variable, scales = "free", nrow = 2, labeller = label_parsed) +
    scale_x_continuous(n.breaks = 3) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Density") +
    theme(legend.position = "right", legend.title = element_text())
}
```

## Sensitivity to the Prior: Perturbation Refits {#sec-supp-perturb}

Power-scaling is a local check. The requirement that matters in practice is global --- that a reasonable analyst with a different prior would publish essentially the same ratings. We therefore refit both posteriors under four joint alternatives for every structural prior: all prior standard deviations doubled, all multiplied by five, and all prior means moved up, or down, by one prior standard deviation. Joint changes can cancel, so each prior group is also widened fivefold on its own. @tbl-supp-perturb-out compares what is published: the power ratings and the resume.

```{r}
sc_joint <- c("Baseline", "SD x 2", "SD x 5", "Means + 1 SD", "Means - 1 SD")
grp_tex <- c(hierarchy = "$\\omega, \\tau$", drift = "$\\phi$", home = "$\\eta$", carry = "$\\beta, \\beta_2$",
             margin = "$\\sigma_m$", efficiency = "$\\lambda, \\sigma_e, \\kappa$", nond1 = "$m_{\\mathrm{nd}}, \\sigma_{\\mathrm{nd}}$")
sc_single <- paste0("SD x 5: ", names(grp_tex))
sc_levels <- c(sc_joint, sc_single)
sc_tex <- c(Baseline = "Baseline", `SD x 2` = "SD $\\times$ 2", `SD x 5` = "SD $\\times$ 5",
            `Means + 1 SD` = "Means $+$1 SD", `Means - 1 SD` = "Means $-$1 SD", setNames(paste0(grp_tex, " sd $\\times$ 5"), sc_single))
ps_rat <- map_dfr(ps_all, \(x) mutate(x$ratings, fit = x$fit, scenario = x$scenario))
ps_pass <- map_dfr(ps_all, \(x) tibble(fit = x$fit, scenario = x$scenario, pass = x$pass))
perturb_summary <- function(rat) {
  base <- rat |> filter(scenario == "Baseline") |> select(fit, team_id, r0 = rating, w0 = wab, wr0 = wab_rank)
  rat |> filter(scenario != "Baseline") |>
    inner_join(base, by = c("fit", "team_id")) |>
    group_by(fit, scenario) |>
    summarise(rho_power = cor(rating, r0, method = "spearman"), mad_power = mean(abs(rating - r0)), max_power = max(abs(rating - r0)),
              rho_wab = cor(wab, w0, method = "spearman"), max_wab = max(abs(wab - w0)), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(fit = factor(fit, levels = c("first", "final")), scenario = factor(scenario, levels = sc_levels)) |>
    arrange(fit, scenario)
}
perturb_all <- perturb_summary(ps_rat)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-supp-perturb-out
#| tbl-cap: "Effect of the prior on the published products, relative to the baseline prior, all Division I teams. Power: Spearman correlation of the ratings, and the mean and largest absolute change in a team's rating (per 100 possessions). Resume: Spearman correlation of $\\WAB$ and the largest absolute change in a team's $\\WAB$. \\emph{Gates}: whether the refit passed them."
perturb_all |>
  left_join(ps_pass |> mutate(fit = factor(fit, levels = c("first", "final")), scenario = factor(scenario, levels = sc_levels)), by = c("fit", "scenario")) |>
  mutate(Fit = ifelse(scenario == "SD x 2", sub("^[0-9-]+, ", "", fit_lab[as.character(fit)]), ""), Prior = sc_tex[as.character(scenario)]) |>
  transmute(Fit, Prior, `$\\rho$ power` = fmt(rho_power, 4), `Mean $|\\Delta|$` = fmt(mad_power, 2), `Max $|\\Delta|$` = fmt(max_power, 2),
            `$\\rho$ WAB` = fmt(rho_wab, 4), `Max $|\\Delta\\WAB|$` = fmt(max_wab, 2), Gates = ifelse(pass, "pass", "fail")) |>
  ktab(align = "llrrrrrl")
pf <- perturb_all |> filter(fit == "final", scenario %in% sc_joint)
p1 <- perturb_all |> filter(fit == "first", scenario %in% sc_joint)
ps1 <- perturb_all |> filter(scenario %in% sc_single) |> group_by(fit) |> slice_max(max_power, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
```

At the end of the season the prior is immaterial to what is published: under every joint alternative the power ratings correlate with the baseline at $\rho \ge `r fmt(min(pf$rho_power), 4)`$, no team's rating moves by more than `r fmt(max(pf$max_power), 2)` points per 100, and no team's $\WAB$ by more than `r fmt(max(pf$max_wab), 2)`. On the first Monday the ratings move more, as they should when the priors carry the fit: by up to `r fmt(max(p1$max_power), 1)` points per 100 (mean `r fmt(max(p1$mad_power), 2)`), with rank correlation at least `r fmt(min(p1$rho_power), 3)`. `r { gf <- as.character(ps1$scenario[ps1$fit == "final"]); g1 <- as.character(ps1$scenario[ps1$fit == "first"]); if (gf == g1) paste0("One prior group at a time, the largest effect in both fits comes from widening the prior on ", grp_tex[sub("SD x 5: ", "", gf)], " (", fmt(ps1$max_power[ps1$fit == "final"], 2), " points at most at the end of the season, ", fmt(ps1$max_power[ps1$fit == "first"], 2), " on the first Monday).") else paste0("One prior group at a time, the largest effect in the final fit comes from widening the prior on ", grp_tex[sub("SD x 5: ", "", gf)], " (", fmt(ps1$max_power[ps1$fit == "final"], 2), " points at most), and on the first Monday from the prior on ", grp_tex[sub("SD x 5: ", "", g1)], " (", fmt(ps1$max_power[ps1$fit == "first"], 2), ").") }` `r { pp <- ps_pass |> filter(scenario != "Baseline"); nf <- pp |> filter(!pass); if (nrow(nf)) paste0(nrow(nf), " of the ", nrow(pp), " refits fail a convergence gate, ", if (all(nf$fit == "final")) "all of them refits of the final posterior, " else "", "and their changes are included in the ranges above; with chains this long a failed gate means slower mixing, not a different posterior.") else "Every refit passes the gates." }` The pooled priors therefore stabilise the sampler in data-poor weeks (@sec-priors) without determining what is published once the season is under way.

## Simulation-based Calibration {#sec-supp-sbc}

The checks so far ask whether the model fits the data. Simulation-based calibration asks whether the *computation* recovers the model: if parameters are drawn from the prior, data simulated from them, and the posterior computed, then the rank of each true value among the posterior draws is uniform when the sampler and the code are correct [@taltsValidatingBayesianInference2018; @modrakSimulationBasedCalibration2023]. We simulate `r n_distinct(sbc$ranks$sim)` seasons on the real structure of the `r sl(last_full)` snapshot of `r format(sbc$snap_date, "%B %e")` --- its `r fmt(sbc$n_teams)` teams, conferences, preseason predictions, `r fmt(sbc$n_games)` games with their weights and missing efficiency margins, and the non-Division I games --- each with its own hyperparameters, team effects, random walk, efficiency margins and margins drawn as the model specifies, refit each with two chains of 500 draws, and rank the true values among `r sbc$n_rank` thinned draws. Besides the structural parameters the test quantities include what is published: every team's centred rating at the snapshot date, its power rank, and its $\WAB$ against the `r ord(sbc$bench)`-best team (the true value computed from the true strengths and the simulated results).

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-sbc
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Simulation-based calibration, ", n_distinct(sbc$ranks$sim), " simulated seasons. Histograms of the rank of the true value among ", sbc$n_rank, " posterior draws, in 10 bins; the band is the central 99\\% range of a bin count under uniformity (for the team-level quantities, pooled over all teams, so the band is narrow). The label gives the coverage of the central 80\\% posterior interval.")'
#| fig-scap: "Simulation-based calibration"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.8
sbc_r <- sbc$ranks |> mutate(bin = pmin(floor(rank / ((sbc$n_rank + 1) / 10)), 9))
sbc_lab <- c(pm_lab, `Power rating` = "Power~rating", `Power rank` = "Power~rank", WAB = "WAB")
sbc_lab <- sbc_lab[names(sbc_lab) %in% unique(sbc$ranks$quantity)]
sbc_cnt <- sbc_r |> count(quantity, bin) |> group_by(quantity) |> mutate(N = sum(n)) |> ungroup()
sbc_band <- sbc_cnt |> distinct(quantity, N) |> mutate(lo = qbinom(0.005, N, 0.1), hi = qbinom(0.995, N, 0.1))
sbc_cov <- sbc_r |> group_by(quantity) |> summarise(cov = mean(covered), .groups = "drop")
sbc_chi <- sbc_cnt |> group_by(quantity) |> summarise(p = pchisq(sum((n - N / 10)^2 / (N / 10)), df = 9, lower.tail = FALSE), .groups = "drop")
fac <- function(q) factor(q, levels = names(sbc_lab), labels = sbc_lab)
ggplot(sbc_cnt |> mutate(q = fac(quantity))) +
  geom_rect(data = sbc_band |> mutate(q = fac(quantity)), aes(xmin = -0.5, xmax = 9.5, ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = col_faint, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_col(aes(bin, n), fill = col_power, alpha = 0.85, width = 0.9) +
  geom_text(data = sbc_cov |> mutate(q = fac(quantity)), aes(x = 4.5, y = Inf, label = paste0("80%: ", round(100 * cov))), vjust = 1.3, size = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(~q, scales = "free_y", ncol = 5, labeller = label_parsed) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Rank of the true value (10 bins)", y = "Count")
team_q <- c("Power rating", "WAB", "Power rank")
sbc_div <- sbc$ranks |> distinct(sim, divergences) |> summarise(d = sum(divergences > 0))
```

The structural parameters are recovered with coverage of the 80\% interval between `r pct(min(sbc_cov$cov[!sbc_cov$quantity %in% team_q]))` and `r pct(max(sbc_cov$cov[!sbc_cov$quantity %in% team_q]))`, and for the published quantities it is `r { q <- sbc_cov$quantity[sbc_cov$quantity %in% team_q]; paste0(ifelse(q == "WAB", "$\\WAB$", tolower(q)), " ", pct(sbc_cov$cov[sbc_cov$quantity %in% team_q]), collapse = ", ") }`. `r { bad <- sbc_chi |> filter(p < 0.01); if (nrow(bad)) paste0("A chi-square test of uniformity of the rank histograms rejects at the 1% level for ", paste(bad$quantity, collapse = ", "), "; with ", fmt(sbc$n_teams), " team-level values per simulated season the team-level tests are very sensitive, and the rank statistics of different teams in one simulation are not independent, so the size of the departure, visible in the figure, matters more than its significance.") else "A chi-square test of uniformity does not reject for any quantity at the 1% level." }` `r if (sbc_div$d == 0) "No simulated fit had a divergent transition." else paste0(sbc_div$d, " of the simulated fits had divergent transitions.")` Ranks are discrete, so ties between a true rank and the posterior draws are broken at random.

#| comment: ""

# Appendix: Reproducibility {#sec-repro .appendix}

The published pipeline is run with `targets::tar_make()` from the project root, after setting an API key for CollegeBasketballData.com; the first full build fits all `r fmt(n_snap + 1)` posteriors in one to two hours on sixteen cores, and later runs fit only new snapshots. The analyses of this paper and the paper itself are targets defined in `_targets.R` and `R/08_analysis.R`, built with `CBB_PAPER=1 Rscript -e 'targets::tar_make()'` (several more hours) and rerun whenever their inputs change. Every number and figure is read from the store and nothing is refitted at render time.

**Randomness.** Every fit uses a fixed seed (2026 for the published fits and most analyses, $2026 + i$ for the $i$-th simulation-based calibration season and for each ablation snapshot, and a seed per step for the replicated data and bootstraps), so a rebuild on the same data and software reproduces every number.

**Software.** R package versions are recorded in `renv.lock` at the project root; @tbl-software lists the main ones and CmdStan.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-software
#| tbl-cap: "Software versions used for this render."
pk <- c("targets", "tarchetypes", "cmdstanr", "posterior", "loo", "priorsense", "dplyr", "ggplot2", "igraph")
tibble::tibble(
  Component = c("R", "CmdStan", pk),
  Version = c(paste(R.version$major, R.version$minor, sep = "."),
              tryCatch(as.character(cmdstanr::cmdstan_version()), error = \(e) "--"),
              map_chr(pk, \(p) tryCatch(as.character(packageVersion(p)), error = \(e) "--")))
) |>
  ktab(align = "ll")
```

**Data.** The providers revise past data occasionally (late score corrections, reclassified games, new betting lines), so a rebuild months later need not reproduce this paper exactly. Every raw file is cached under `data/raw/` and never re-fetched once a season is final, which is the snapshot the paper was built from; @tbl-data-hash records, for each season, what the models saw and a hash of it. This build read the data on `r format(dh$built[1], "%Y-%m-%d")`.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-data-hash
#| tbl-cap: "The data behind this build, by season: Division I teams, completed Division I and non-Division I games, Division I games with an efficiency margin and with a closing line, snapshots, and an xxHash64 hash of the season's games table as the models read it."
dh |>
  transmute(Season = sl(season), Teams = d1_teams, `D-I games` = fmt(d1_games), `Non-D-I` = fmt(nond1_games),
            `With eff.` = fmt(with_eff), `With line` = fmt(with_line), Snapshots = snapshots, Hash = paste0("\\texttt{", hash, "}")) |>
  ktab(align = "lrrrrrrl")
```
